historical_grapheme_analysis.finding: Steffel <tsch> represents the voiceless palatoalveolar affricate [č]; <tsch> and <ts> are analyzed as allophones of /č/ in the historical system.
historical_grapheme_analysis.status: phonetic normalization, not a newly inferred sound change

independent_correspondence_controls.role: independent modern phonological/lexical control showing historical <tsch>/č corresponding to modern tʃ in the same lexical family
independent multi-variety lexical control for historical initial č ~ modern orthographic ch in the black-color family

target_formal_comparison.stress_alignment: SRC-02 Chipérami and historical tschipérameke both mark stress on the same stem syllable -pér-
target_formal_comparison.suffix_interpretation: belongs to the broader ame-centered participial/derivational research problem; no lexeme-specific one-step change is assumed

semantic_evidence.historical: Fein. Dünn. Flach. / fine, thin, flat
semantic_evidence.independent_community_2010: chiperami occurs in a Guerrero bilingual riddle aligned with Spanish ‘parezco tablilla’; semantic value is contextual, compatible with flat/thin/board-like
semantic_evidence.same_lineage_2016_refinement: kusí pus chipérami jiti = ‘con un palo ancho’
semantic_evidence.additional_public_modern_usage: kawí chipérami occurs in a context contrasting an old belief that the earth was flat with chitúlami for circular/round
semantic_evidence.assessment: semantic continuity in the flat/broad/thin domain is very strong, while independence levels differ by source

independence_assessment.other_semantic_corroboration: 2016 dictionary is Hilton-lineage; public religious translation has unaudited lexical provenance

why_grade_A: The historical affricate value is source-analyzed, not guessed from German spelling.
Historical <tsch>/č to modern tʃ/ch is independently supported by the sleep and black lexical families before applying it to Tſchiper.
The target's stem-like string and stress align closely: čipér- ~ chipér-.
The flat/thin semantic domain is stable across Steffel, SRC-02 and independent community usage.
An independent modern community witness exists outside the unresolved SRC-02/Hilton lineage.
remaining_limits: Grade A measures evidential architecture, not demonstrated cognacy.
The historical form is not reduced to a bare lexeme čipér unless a source explicitly attests/analyzes that base; stem-like string is used descriptively.
The exact historical pathway from -ameke to modern -ami is not solved at the lexeme level.
The SEP community text does not itself assign a Pp category or an isolated dictionary gloss to chiperami.
Modern SRC-02 orthography is not treated as a validated phonemic transcription.
next_tests: Search for a historical or modern bare/base chiper-like form and explicit derivational analyses.
Map chiperami across additional communities and modern descriptions.
Use the color and Compendio data to model the history of -ameke/-ame/-ami separately from the very strong root correspondence.
